text: Good afternoon, everyone. I call the September 9th, 2026, Legislative and Policy Committee meeting to order. Sign-ups for in-person public comments occurred prior to the start of the committee meeting. Do we have any sign-ups today? Seeing none. Thank you. We'll move on to the next item of the agenda. Before doing so, I'll note that Mrs. Griffiths should be joining us in just a few minutes, but we will go ahead and take

a look at the draft minutes. Dr. Rashid, have you had an opportunity to take a look at the draft minutes for the August 12th meeting? I did, and I have no amendments or changes to it. Thank you. And do we have a motion to approve the minutes? So moved to approve the minutes. I will second the motion. All in favor of approving the minutes for the August 12th, 2026, meeting say, "Aye." Aye. Aye. All opposed?

The motion to approve the minutes passes two to zero with all school board members present voting yes, and Mrs. Griffiths absent for the vote. And with that, we will move on to our first action item, which is item 4.01, Policy 1010: School Division Legal Status. I will turn it over to Dr.

Bergen to discuss that action item. Thank you, Chair Svenson. Board members, how are you tonight? Good. Good to see you both. This, of course, is returning to you from action from your last meeting. Policy 1010, School Division Legal Status, is due for its five-year review, and it would be our recommendation that you consider the proposed changes that were presented at your last meeting and then take action to forward the revisions to the

full school board. But before taking the action, I'll just take a minute to review some of the feedback we received. All of the feedback for our listening public is attached online. There's a summary in front of you board members, which I'll read from for you. We did have feedback from MSAC, LEAF, and the Equity Committee. MSAC's feedback on this particular policy occurred at lines 20 through 22,

and they were referencing that section that says, "If the school board believes the law adopted by the General Assembly of Virginia to be unconstitutional, how would the board then proceed?" Really more of a question or a comment than a suggestion on a revision to the policy. At line 11, LEAF asked, for rezoning purposes, how often this occurs

because there is a reference within the policy of the state creating the boundaries for the various school divisions in the Commonwealth. And similarly, the Equity Committee asked if the Board of Education is responsible for school and division zoning , which it was unclear to me if they were asking if they meant within the boundaries of Loudoun County or if we have some ability to change our boundaries with our neighboring school divisions.

At any rate, staff doesn't have any recommendations for any revisions to this Policy 1010 based upon this feedback. I would just share, we appreciate the feedback from all of our advisories, and in response to LEAF and the Equity Committee asking about rezoning, at least at the state level. The Constitution of Virginia Article 8, Section 5, states that the powers and duties of the Board of Education shall be as

follows, bullet point A, subject to such criteria and conditions as the General Assembly may prescribe. The board, meaning the State Board of Education, shall divide the Commonwealth into school divisions of such geographical area and school-age population as will promote the realization of prescribed standards of quality and shall periodically review the adequacy of existing school divisions for this purpose. At least the Constitution did not define

periodically. So again, staff has no proposed revisions to this policy, and we will turn it over to you, Chair Svenson, for any action the committee may wish to take. Thank you, Dr. Bergen. Yes, I read the feedback. Maybe two were referring to rezoning locally, and I can see why there might be some confusion reading it. But just for clarity, the policy is referring to the dividing up the school divisions across the state, so we have Loudoun County,

Prince William, et cetera. So appreciate the feedback on that point. Do my fellow members have any comments on Policy 1010, School Division Legal Status? All right. Then we will go ahead and take a vote. So I'll first ask if there's a motion to

move this policy forward to the full board. Yes. Yes, Dr. Rashid. Thank you, Chair. I'd like to move Policy 1010, School Division Legal Status, to the full board. Thank you, Dr. Rashid. Is there a second? Second. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. And I think the motion, Dr. Rashid, you said that the Legislative and Policy Committee

consider proposed changes to Policy 1010 and forward it to the full school board as an information item. Yes, I confirm that. Okay. And you second that motion, Mrs. Griffiths? Yes. Thank you. All right. With that, we will take a vote. All in favor say, "Aye." Aye. Aye. Aye. All right, all three school board members voted yes, and the motion passes. Policy 1010 will go to the full school board as an information item.

With that, we'll move on to item 4.02, Policy 1035: School Board Norms, Protocols, and Violations. I will again turn it over to Dr. Bergen. Thank you, Chair Svenson. Policy 1035 was adopted in April of 2021, and the proposed changes in the red line that were before the committee at your last meeting align with our current practice and provide additional clarity.

The policy was last reviewed in December of 2025 by the former LA&P Committee and had been forwarded to the school board, which forwarded it back to this committee for further review. There were quite a bit of feedback on this policy as well from our various advisories. And so before I share that feedback, again, it would be our recommendation from administration that the Legislative and Policy Committee consider the proposed

changes to Policy 1035 and forward to the full school board as an information item. We also have some recommended changes for your consideration should you care to take up an amendment based upon the feedback. MSAC, at lines 24 and 25 of the red line, referenced that there are various roles and responsibilities of the school board, and their comment was that other members of the school division and staff also have

various roles in addition to the school board members. They didn't explicitly state, but I think it was implied that perhaps we would reference that others, other than the school board, have various roles to play. We are not making that recommendation for that change in administration, but you're certainly welcome to take that up as a committee. Both MSAC and the Equity Council referenced some duplicative language in the policy. So at line 79 to 87, under the paragraph for professional development,

the language tracks almost precisely with the language at lines excuse me, 184 to 190. MSAC also, in that same section at the end of the professional development section, at lines 84 and 85, noted that there is a conflict between "to the extent possible" and "shall."

MSAC also referenced at lines 197 to 198, the use of the word "may" indicates that a school board member may not face any reprimand if found in violation of the school board norms and protocols, so their recommendation was to change the word "may" to "shall." And the Equity Committee provided some feedback that they had heard from teachers that yearly professional development can sometimes be repetitive and does not

include other professional development, which should be necessary, such as including cultural competency, and training should be effective and geared towards areas needing improvement. Considering all of the feedback from the advisories, the administration would recommend that the committee consider striking lines 184 to 190

and amending at line 79 under paragraph B, professional development, as prescribed by the Virginia Standards of Quality, which was about the one standalone phrase that existed in 184 to 190 that's not underneath professional development. So if you were to entertain that, that paragraph would begin, "As prescribed by the Virginia Standards of Quality, each member of the school board." Then further along in that section at line 84,

with the recommendation from MSAC, we would ask the committee to consider striking to the extent possible and leave shall in place. That's all the feedback that I have to give, and I'll turn it back over to you, Chair Stenson. Thank you, Dr. Bergen. School members, any feedback, comments on this policy?

I do know if I can bring about amendments, but I did not have any feedback. Okay. Yes. Well, maybe we can do the base motion, and then we can do some amendments. So just for simplicity, I will make the motion. I move that the legislative and policy committee consider proposed changes to Policy 1035 and forward it to the full school board as an information item. Do I have a second?

Second. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. The motion's been made by myself and seconded by Mrs. Griffiths. Now we will entertain any amendments. Dr. Rashid. Thank you, Chair Stenson. I had teams, both my colleagues here, on two separate threads, indicating for Policy 1035, the red line version below, and this coincides with what MSAC is recommending. There's two portions, and that is one for...

So I move to amend Policy 1035 red line version to change the word may to shall in lines 197 and 198. So I'm going from down now, so that it reads, quote, "If a majority of the school board members find a violation has occurred, the school board shall issue one or more of the following or direct the board chair to do so on behalf of the board." Unquote. So as it's currently written, it is possible for a school board member to

misconstrue or misunderstand this and in fact, not face any reprimand, even though they have been found in violation. And then I have another one, but I'll wait. Thank you. I appreciate splitting those up. Do folks have feedback, comments on that proposed amendment to change that language from may to shall? Yes, Mrs. Griffiths. Thank you, Chair Stenson. So for this policy,

per Ms. Rashid's amendment, this is if we don't do the training, if I'm understanding this right, if we don't proceed with the training, is that what that's about? And forgive me, I came in late, so I'm just trying to... I'm happy to step in, and maybe Mr. Allen, you can step in if you have something additional to add. My understanding is that the section that Dr.

Rashid's proposing to amend, the violation section, applies to the whole policy, so it would be any violation, not just professional development, just if a majority of the school board member found another to be in violation. So that would mean what we're adding, it's 79 to 87, which is red line. If a school board member did not do the training, they're in violation. Can somebody explain that to me? That's what it looks like.

Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. I can hop in. That's one part of it. So this policy provides guidance to school board members for all the norms, protocols, and the code of conduct, which is 1030. And so it's any perceived violation that the board determines would then potentially, if I understand Dr. Rashid's proposed amendment correctly, would require

then the school board to address that school board member who they found violated any of the norms or protocols to include the training, but for any of this or any potential violation of the code of conduct, again, that's Policy 1030, would then the school board would be required to render one of these options to address that violation. If I may. The reason why I bring that up is because we already had 1035.

We're adding that red line, which is new. So that's why I bring it up, because that is a new paragraph that we're adding to this document. So we should've been following this policy all along, but now we're adding the training in there as well. So that's why I was concerned and why I brought it up. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. Just as a point of clarification, that language that you

see there on line 77 through 87, that is duplicative, or it's pretty much the same rather as Section 8, on page five, on lines 184 through 190. So there's already a requirement for school board members to participate annually in high-quality professional development activities. And for instance, that includes the VSBA trainings that you do in November.

So you are already doing those. Thank you for the clarification. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. Dr. Rashid, I realize that maybe I should have given you the opportunity to speak to your motion if there's a reason that you support changing the may to shall. Appreciate that, Chair Stenson, and no worries. I bring this about also because I think it holds school board members accountable,

myself included, and it just makes it more definitive. Thank you. Thank you, Dr. Rashid. I definitely appreciate the goal of ensuring that we have accountability for fellow school board members. I struggle a little bit with changing from may to shall just for limiting the flexibility with how to handle a particular violation. Maybe the majority of the school board thinks the violation is technical in nature

and doesn't necessitate one of these admonitions. So I'm thinking through the amendment, but I welcome thoughts from if you have anything further you'd like to add, or Mrs. Griffiths, any additional comments. Yes, ma'am. Thank you, Chair Stenson. Yeah, I tend to agree with you there on that particular amendment. Thank you. All right. If nothing further, why don't we take a vote? And Dr.

Rashid, for clarity, could you read the amendment again? Thank you. Thank you, Chair. I move to amend Policy 1035 red line version to change the word may to shall in lines 197 to 198 so that it reads, quote, "If a majority of the school board members find a violation has occurred, the school board shall issue one or more of the following or direct the board chair to do so on behalf of the board." Unquote.

And then I will second the amendment. So it's on the floor here. And then with that, I think we'll move forward to a vote. All in favor of Dr. Rashid's amendment, say aye. Aye. Those opposed, say nay. Nay. Nay. The motion fails two to one with Dr. Rashid in support and myself and Mrs. Griffiths opposed. With that, we'll move back to the base motion. I think, Dr. Rashid, you have an additional amendment.

Yes. Thank you, Chair. In the same policy, Policy 1035 red line version, I move to amend in lines 84 to 85, delete the opening phrase, quote, unquote, "To the extent possible," unquote, and changing the sentence to read, quote, "The school board shall hold such a session jointly for all members on an annual basis." Unquote. I will second that amendment.

And would you like to speak to your amendment? Sure. Thank you, Chair. Again, not much, it's pretty self-explanatory, but just changing the phrase gives more clarity that's required, and it just, again, makes it just more definitive. Thank you. Any feedback, comments on-- Mr. Allen, do you have one way in? Yes, just for clarity, this specific provision is not required by the Virginia

Standards of Quality or SOQs, that's set forth in 22.1-253.13:5, Section D, and it would require if the school board jointly has such a session, that would be subject to open meeting requirements under FOIA. And I don't know what the school board has contemplated, if that be in the form of a retreat or otherwise, but I just did want to share that consideration because

that would be a change in practice. Is there some tension in the language there currently to the extent possible in shall, or do we think that is reconcilable? Thank you for the question. Chair Sensen, I tend to agree that that tension is kind of glaring, and then so I think it should be addressed.

I just point out the underlying consideration that this is a new practice from what is currently in policy, and it's not required in law, so it'd be certainly within the board's well to do so, but wanted to point that out for consideration. Mrs. Griffiths. Thank you, Chair Sensen. And in regards to that, I'm going to say maybe we just keep it as is

and not remove to the extent possible. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. For consideration, the board could make it, or this committee could recommend that it be aspirational, so you could strike the "to the extent possible" and revise the language "The school board shall endeavor to hold such a session," then it leaves it in the school board as aspirational.

Dr. Rasheed, since it's your amendment, thoughts on that proposal? Just for clarification, Mr. Allen, if you can repeat that phrase again, because I'm trying to see if it's just a synonym to the extent possible. That's all. Thank you, Dr. Rasheed. I think it captures it's more aspirational rather than to the extent possible.

To the extent possible is to the extent it's-- There could be various reasons that it's not possible in terms of scheduling or otherwise. But I see your point, and I think it's for the committee to consider. Okay. And then for that reason, I think my amendment still stands as is. Thank you. And Dr. Rasheed, I was wondering

if we were to have the mandatory professional development as a group, if you're envisioning us having our current retreat transformed into more of a professional development setting, or thoughts about that. Yes, the latter would be perfectly fine. I didn't look at this more as an individual basis, but yes, as a session would be fine. Any type of annual basis, be it in whatever form, is what I'm amenable to.
And altogether as a group. Absolutely.

Could you read your amendment again? No problem. Thank you. I move to amend policy 1035 red line version to read in lines 84 to 85, delete the opening phrase, quote, "To the extent possible," unquote, and changing the sentence to read, quote, "The school board shall hold such a session jointly for all members on an annual basis." Unquote.

Thank you. I think any further discussion on this? All right. We will take a vote. All in favor of Dr. Rasheed's amendment say aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed? Nay. Amendment passes two to one, with Dr. Rasheed, myself voting yes, and Mrs. Griffiths voting no. The base motion has been amended accordingly. At this time, I'd like to ask

if there's a motion to support staff's recommendation to strike lines 184 to 190 in the proposed red lines to policy 1035 on the basis that such language is generally duplicative of the language in lines 79 to 87, 184 to 190. I'm sorry, Chair. I'm a little unclear.

Maybe I missed this line. Was this something that you're pertaining to of those lines that you're recalling? Yeah. So, when Dr. Bergen was presenting, there was discussion from some of the advisory committees that lines 184 to 190 of the red line version are duplicative of our new professional development section up at lines 79 to 87. delete lines 184 to 190, because it is duplicative of lines 79 to 87. Okay. Is that-- Are you- Is there a motion to do that? So moved. Is there a second? I will second. Any further discussion on that? All right. All in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed? Nay.

The amendment passes two to one with Dr. Rasheed and myself in support, and Mrs. Griffiths opposed. So now the base motion has been amended to strike those duplicative lines on 184 to 190. I think that with that, is there any more discussion on the base motion?

All right. With that- Chair Sensen. Yes, Dr. Bergen. If I could just check in with division counsel. When we strike-- If the committee were to strike paragraph eight, the only reference in paragraph eight that doesn't repeat in professional development is the reference to the Virginia Standards of Quality. So, part of staff recommendation would be to carry that phrase into the intro to the professional development paragraph. I don't know that it's necessary.

I'm just asking, does the additional reference to the standards of quality give that more weight? Thank you for the question, Dr. Bergen. Because there is a legal reference to the Virginia Standards of Quality, I don't see that it's necessary. It's certainly within the committee's purview and ultimately the school board's purview. What I would point out is this legal reference, which is 22.1-253.13:7, should be replaced.

It should be 13:5, Section D, which I was going to propose as a technical amendment down the road, but since we're talking about it, you all could consider that right now to clarify that. Thank you, Dr. Bergen, and thank you, Mr. Allen. I will make an amend-- And so just to clarify, you're referring to the cross
reference 22.1-253.13:7? Yes, which should be 13:5 instead of :7. Okay. I move to amend the policy 1035 to remove the cross reference, or to replace the cross reference 22.1-253.13:7 with

22.1/253.13:5, Section D of the Code of Virginia. Is there a second? Second. Thank you, Dr. Rashid. I've made the motion to amend the cross-reference. Dr. Rashid has seconded. Is there any discussion on the update to the cross-reference? All in favor of this amendment say aye. Aye.

Aye. All opposed? The amendment passes three to zero with all school board members present voting yes. And now we'll go back to the base motion as amended. Is there any further discussion? Yes, Mrs. Griffith. If I could just get clarification, you were talking about line eight, Mr. Allen? Of the red line? Thank you, Mrs. Griffith. Section eight.

Or line eight. Section eight or line eight? It's section D8. Oh, okay. So it's lines 184 to 180. Yep. And let me go back to that. And what were you referencing, please? Certainly. Dr. Bergen was mentioning on line 184, that starts out

that section, "The Virginia Standards of Quality provide that each school board must require its members to participate annually in high-quality professional development activities..." As we discussed earlier, the proposed section B that's on lines 77 through 88 on page two substantively tracks that language except for it doesn't call out the Virginia Standards of Quality.

Okay. So, are we going to amend and add that back, the Virginia Standards of Quality? I think the recommendation was, or the advice was we didn't necessarily need to. That is where that obligation stems from, but I don't know if we necessarily have to have that language in. Okay. If we don't need it, that's fine. I was looking in the wrong section, so I didn't know what you were talking about. So now I know. So thank you so much.

Thank you, Mrs. Griffith. And if no further discussion, we'll take a vote on Policy 1035. So the motion on the floor, I will move that the Legislative and Policy Committee consider proposed changes to Policy 1035 as amended and forward it to the full school board as an information item. Just for the record, is there a second for that? Second. Thank you, Dr. Rashid. And we'll take a vote now.

All in favor of the motion say aye. Aye. Aye. Those say nay, nay. And we now have the motion passes two to one with Dr. Rashid and myself voting yes and Mrs. Griffith voting no, that 1035 will go to the full school board as an information item. All right. Now we'll move to action item

4.03, which is Policy 7712, Sick Leave. I'll put the base motion on the floor. I'll move that the Legislative and Policy Committee consider proposed changes to Policy 7712 and forward it to the full school board as an information item. Is there a second for that motion? Second.

Thank you. And with that motion on the floor, I just wanted to turn it over to Ms. Brown to present any additional information on it. Good evening. Thank you so much. We did receive some feedback on this policy. A few work clarifications requested. The definition of suspicious pattern was asked and a question about references to

bereavement leave. There were also concerns raised about requiring employees to repay overused sick leave and limiting leave whenever a substitute is unavailable. So at this point in time, staff does not recommend any changes to the revised policy that we have presented. All references to bereavement policy have been removed because we are hoping to establish a standalone bereavement policy. Employee's ability to use sick leave when a substitute is not available applies

only to when sick leave is utilized for personal leave. And at this time, our intent is to align this policy with the newly established CBA sick leave policy. And so the provisions regarding sick leave payouts upon separation, those types of things, were not contemplated in this current revision.

Thank you, Ms. Brown. And board members, any questions on this policy? No. All right. Thank you very much for putting this policy together, and conforming it to the policy under the CBA. Appreciate that effort. We will go ahead and take a vote. All school board members in favor of considering proposed changes to Policy 7712 and forwarding it to the full school board as information item, say

aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed, say nay. The motion passes three to zero with all school board members present voting yes. With that, we'll move to item 4.04, which is Policy 7713, Bereavement Leave. I will just put the motion on the floor. I move that the Legislative and Policy Committee consider new Policy 7713 and

forward it to the full school board as an information item. Is there a second? Second. Thank you, Mrs. Griffith. I've made the motion, and it's been seconded by Mrs. Griffith. With that, I will turn it over to Ms. Brown to speak about this bereavement leave policy. So this policy establishes bereavement leave for those who are not covered under collective bargaining agreements. And the feedback that we received was largely positive. There was only one concern raised, and that was about the potential misuse without the requirement of documentation.

And at this point in time, we do not recommend any changes to the revised policy. Employees, whenever they submit for this type of leave, can provide documentation and can provide additional information should they choose through our current system. And so I believe that should they choose to disclose more information, there is a mechanism in place for them to do so. Thank you, Ms. Brown. Board members, any questions or comments? No. All right.

With that, we will take a vote. All in favor of the motion that the Legislative and Policy Committee consider new Policy 7713 and forward it to the full school board as an information item, say aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed, say nay. The motion passes three to zero with all school board members present voting yes. With that, we have completed our action items. We are now moving to information

item 5.01, Policy 3130, Evaluation, and I will turn it over to Dr. Bergen to present on evaluation. Thank you, Chair Svenson, and as we shift out of action, Ms. Brown has another commitment, so we thank her for her time and joining the committee today. Okay. Evaluation Policy 3130 is up for its five-year review.

There are minor revisions as shown up on the screen, consistent with changes we've made to other policies, striking the word division in front of superintendent at lines four and seven, and just for clarity, inserting at line 11 that the purpose of this policy is to guide the superintendent's evaluation. Staff has no other recommended changes. Open to questions. Thank you, Dr. Bergen. Board members, any questions?

No. All right. With that, then, I guess I'll take a temperature check if we are comfortable moving this to action at the next LMP meeting. Second that, yes. It looks like everyone's comfortable with that. So we'll move this to the action item for the next Legislative and Policy Committee meeting. And we'll go ahead and put it out for review by the community and bring you back any feedback. Thank you very much, Dr. Bergen.

And next, we are going to go to item 5.02, which is our legislative update from Mr. Sutton. I'm looking forward to hearing the update about our plans for the upcoming legislative session, and looking forward, especially hearing how the roundtable went, hearing from community members here at LCPS. So Mr. Sutton. Thank you so much. Appreciate it Good afternoon, Mr. Chairman, board members. Thank you for the opportunity to provide an update on Loudoun County Public

Schools' proposed legislative priorities for the upcoming 2027 Virginia General Assembly session, as well as an overview of our upcoming legislative breakfast. As we prepare for the 2027 General Assembly, LCPS has taken a deliberate, collaborative approach to identifying the issues we believe are most important to our students, families, educators, and community. Rather than developing a legislative agenda in isolation, we engaged a diverse

group of 42 participants from across the school division and the broader community. This group included parents, students, principals, cabinet members, and departmental staff, bringing a wide range of experiences and perspectives to the conversation. We convened a stakeholder roundtable to create an intentional opportunity for participants to identify emerging challenges, share experiences,

and discuss potential policy solutions, and help determine the legislative issues that should receive our attention during this upcoming session. The participants engaged in small group discussions, focusing on five areas that have been determined that we can anticipate a lot of discussion and a lot of attention at the 2027

General Assembly session. They are important, and we will hear a lot about them this year. They are school funding, as always, workforce alignment, student mental health and wellbeing, intentional technology, and safe and supportive school environments. We also made a specific effort to incorporate student voices by providing our student participants with targeted questions and

opportunities to share out their experiences and perspectives, which was absolutely amazing. Following the roundtable, our legislative partners had an opportunity to review the feedback, common themes, policy recommendations emerged, and that information helped us refine the proposed legislative priorities that I'm going to talk about today, and that hopefully we're going to bring forward for information on September 22nd to the school board.

The result of the proposed agenda is grounded in experiences of the people we serve and informed by, again, a cross-section of our school division and our community. So let me go through them if I can. At the center of our agenda is the K through 12 education funding and equity. Loudoun County continues to be very large and very diversified, and sustainable state investment is essential if we're going to provide every student with the

resources and opportunities that they need to be successful. We will continue to advocate for sustained investment in several critical areas this year, including student mental health and wellbeing, high-quality and affordable Pre-K, English learner education, and intentional technology infrastructure that's going to be necessary to provide a comprehensive and

equitable education. For early childhood education, we support the funding for high-quality Pre-K. Expanding access to Pre-K gives children an opportunity to develop academic, social, and emotional foundations they need to enter kindergarten and to learn. For our English learner students, we support increased

funding that recognize the staffing, infrastructure, instructional translation, family engagement, counseling, wraparound supports necessary to meet the needs of a growing and increasingly diverse student population. We also will continue to emphasize the importance of adequate and sustainable funding for school operations, staffing, infrastructure, and general programs.

Ultimately, investment allows local school divisions to manage local resources responsibly while maintaining high-quality educational opportunities for our students. Let's talk about secondary and post-secondary access, which is going to be a huge issue this year. This is our second major area that we're going to be talking about, particularly career-connected learning and workforce development. We will continue to advocate for increased support for dual enrollment, technical

training, career readiness initiatives, and youth pre-apprenticeship opportunities. These programs give students the opportunity to explore careers, develop technical and employable skills in our industry-recognized credentials, and gain meaningful work-based learning experiences while they are still in high school. We also see tremendous value in strengthening partnerships among schools,

colleges, businesses, workforce partners, and community organizations. The goal is to work with our legislative partners to create clear pathways from high school into registered apprenticeships, post-secondary education, and high-demand careers, while also helping employers develop a strong pipeline of skilled and work-ready talent. This is an area where education and workforce policy are increasingly

interconnected, and we believe Virginia has an opportunity to make strategic investments that benefit both students and the Commonwealth's economy. Let's talk about student mental health and wellbeing. Again, another issue that is going to be talked about on a large scale this year. LCPS is committed to ensuring that students have access to mental and behavioral health support they need to succeed academically, socially, and

quite frankly, personally. We will advocate for sustainable, recurring funding to expand school-based mental and behavioral health services, strengthen staffing for our school counselors, psychologists, social workers, nurses, behavioral specialists, and other student support professionals. We also support investments in prevention, early identification and screening, suicide prevention, crisis response, mental health awareness, and

professional development for school personnel, because they're on the front line, so that they can really take hold of what's going on. Partnerships are also critical. Schools cannot address issues alone. We need strong partnerships with families, community service boards, health providers, and other community organizations. We also are looking at strengthening Medicaid reimbursement for eligible

school-based mental health services and ensuring that services are responsive and accessible to all of our students and families. That's crucial. And importantly, as Virginia considers new health requirements or initiatives, we believe that mandates must be accompanied by funding, workforce capacity, professional development, and implementation support. Local school divisions, regardless of whether it's Loudoun County or Washington

County, need the resources and flexibility to implement new requirements effectively without diverting resources from those other critical education needs. Let's talk about safe and supportive school environments. Our fourth priority is about safety. Safety is more about physical security, increasingly more about physical security. It also means creating schools where students feel a sense of belonging, where

concerns are identified early, and where students have access to supports that they desperately need. We will advocate for sustainable funding and resources to strengthen our school climate, student connectivity, bullying, cyberbullying prevention, behavioral supports, threat assessment, crisis response, and evidence-based approaches to student discipline. Again, adequate staffing is key, and adequate staffing is central to this work, and

we will continue to advocate for that. School counselors, psychologists, social workers, behavioral specialists, nurses, all these people play an incredible crucial role to identifying concerns early, providing interventions, and connecting students and families with community-based services. So we also support mental health and behavioral health training for school personnel, suicide prevention and crisis intervention initiatives, and

again, strong partnerships among our school family, our community service boards, behavioral health providers, and public safety partners. That is crucial. As with mental health, we believe that any new state requirements also related to school safety and student support need to come with the adequate funding, professional development, implementation of resources, flexibility by our local school divisions.
